cover.title: What Does the Fed Actually Do?

lines.text: 12 people voted in September to raise your card rate.
lines.say: Twelve people voted in September to raise your card rate.

lines.text: That's the Federal Reserve. Its two jobs touch every dollar you have.
lines.say: That's the Federal Reserve. Its two jobs touch every dollar you have.

lines.text: Its goal is 2% inflation. In August 2026, prices rose 3.4% from a year earlier.
lines.say: Its goal is two percent inflation. In August twenty twenty-six, prices rose three point four percent from a year earlier.

lines.text: Its main tool is a target for the rate banks charge each other overnight.
lines.say: Its main tool is a target for the rate banks charge each other overnight.

lines.text: On Sept. 16, 2026, it raised that target to a range of 3.75%-4.00%, the first since 2023.
lines.say: On September sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, it raised that target to a range of three point seven five to four percent, the first since twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: That followed cuts from a 5.5% peak in 2023.
lines.say: That followed cuts from a five point five percent peak in twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: Banks then raised prime to 7%, and most cards charge prime plus a markup.
lines.say: Banks then raised prime to seven percent, and most cards charge prime plus a markup.

lines.text: On $5,000, that quarter point adds about $12.50 a year if the balance stays put.
lines.say: On five thousand dollars, that quarter point adds about twelve dollars and fifty cents a year if the balance stays put.

lines.text: The Fed never lends to you, but it moves what your borrowing costs.
lines.say: The Fed never lends to you, but it moves what your borrowing costs.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: 12 votes that move your credit card rate: the Fed explained
post.ig:
12 people voted in September to raise your card rate.

The Federal Reserve's two jobs from Congress: maximum employment and stable prices (a 2% inflation goal).
CPI inflation was 3.4% year over year in August 2026.
On Sept. 16, 2026, the Fed raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since 2023. Big banks' prime rate went to 7%.
On a $5,000 card balance, a quarter-point rise adds about $12.50 of interest a year if the balance stays put.

Sources: Federal Reserve FOMC statement (Sept 16, 2026), BLS CPI (Aug 2026), bank prime rate announcements (Sept 17, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
